# Description

As a user of the asset list retool, I may want to append a note to an `asset` such that I can identify why an asset is configured the way it is.

For example:  I would like to be able to disable an asset by removing support for all entities.  I should be able to see a note in the Retool explaining why it was disabled.

# **Acceptance Criteria**

* Retool should displace a notes section for each asset. 

# **Dependencies**

I'm guessing this relies on some database to add a note field to the asset definitions .
nodes.title: Asset List retool should have notes for AssetsTypes.

nodes.description:
Running services locally in Kubernetes via Tilt shows non-deterministic startup because services wait for infra dependencies (databases, mailhog, fakegcs, etc.) but not for each other.

Examples observed:

* `assetregistry` crashloops if the `organization` pod is not up yet.
* `blockchain` crashloops if `assetregistry` is down.

Consider reducing `assetregistry` as a single point of failure (e.g., services keeping a persistent copy of assetregistry data until next refresh) so services can restart/operate in a degraded state while dependencies recover.

Slack thread: [https://anchorinc.slack.com/archives/C061FN8EAER/p1771639096880819](<https://anchorinc.slack.com/archives/C061FN8EAER/p1771639096880819>)
nodes.title: Services crashloop on missing dependencies in local k8s (read thread!)

nodes.description:
# Description

Two assets cannot have the same contract address. We need to prevent Asset Registry from allowing the registration of an asset with a contract that matches an existing asset.

Context: [https://anchorinc.slack.com/archives/C08AG2X4UFM/p1771581389059669](<https://anchorinc.slack.com/archives/C08AG2X4UFM/p1771581389059669>)

# **Acceptance Criteria**

* Attempting to add an asset with the contract address that another asset already has should fail with an informative message that includes some information about the conflicting asset
* If a pending operation to create an asset with the same contract exists, the action should fail with an informative message that includes some information about the conflicting asset
nodes.title: Check for Duplicate Contract Address

# Description

When refreshing the types, we should be able to check if the client actually needs to update. This should:

1. Reduce the load on the Asset Registry Database
2. Reduce the data flowing across the wire
3. Reduce the amount of time a service that uses Asset Registry has to spend updating the local cache

### Notes

* Consider ETag type setup like HTTP has?

# **Acceptance Criteria**

* Clients only update the local cache when they:
  * Don't have any data
  * Data has changed
* In the case of a cache hit, very limited data needs to flow across the wire
nodes.title: Don't Update the Cache if no changes

nodes.description:
Piggybacking on the move of watchers to cloud deploy, we want to add the capability to enable networks dynamically. To achieve that, we need to make all the modules and periodic tasks created/enabled dynamically by the enablement of a network.

### Example

At the moment we don't have a clear way to enable a new network, but we can use Retool to these kinds of operations and observe the current state by networks. Regardless, we can think on a few options of what we can do after enabling or disabling a new network: 

​Option 1: the system responds in a sync way when we enable a network, by creating the required periodic tasks and creating the module.

Option 2: the system gets the list of all available networks and by default tries to create the required periodic tasks and modules. If the network is disabled we pause them until a change occurs. For the case of the Modules we can create all of them by default.

Option 3: ?

## Acceptance Criteria

* We are able to enable/create modules and periodic tasks dynamically when a network is enabled or disabled

# Dependencies

This task will cannot move forward until we move all watchers to cloud deploy.
nodes.title: Investigate how Blockchain starts periodic tasks and modules based on enabled networks

# Description

At the moment we use the network regex expression to verify if the onchain identifier that we are adding is valid or not. The problem is that for some token types, like `LSD_APTOS` on Aptos, the onchain identifier has some suffix that is not part of the regex ( `3a30a6e5936c0a4c5140daed34de39d17ca7fcae08f947c02e979cef98a3719:🪙:LSD` - instead of emoji it is : coin : ).

We need to update this to allow users to add a new token with no issues, but we need to decide if we change the regex, add a new one specific for tokens or remove the validation in specific cases.

# **Acceptance Criteria**

* We are able to add tokens where the onchain identifiers have specific nomenclature

# **Dependencies**

* FE help

nodes.description:
Now, that we only use the `ANCHOR_ASSET_TYPES_ENABLED` at production level to manage native assets/networks we can rename and make everything more network related instead of think of it as a source for the required network.

* rename the env variable from asset to network
  * Suggestions
    * `ANCHOR_REGISTERED_NETWORKS`
    * `ANCHOR_SUPPORTED_NETWORKS`
    * Ask Claude for better naming options
* change the ids to a network id
  * example: ETH_R -> ETHEREUM_REGNET
* change the asset registry code to handle directly the networks instead of converting assets into it (eg. logic_v2.go)

⚠️ this task should not handle changes to the environment variable used for tests purposes

## Acceptance Criteria

* No more references to enablement, it's about available networks
* Similar purpose, different env variable name
* Should help make it clear what is happening with this
* Update Notion with the new variable and as part of [PROC-3709](https://linear.app/anchorlabs/issue/PROC-3709/update-asset-enablement-documentation)

# Description

The Remote Fetcher refresh cron is always registering assets independently if the asset is already in the global state map, so we need to include a validation to cases where we try to update an asset where the network and token type mismatch between what already exists.

This was an existing validation before the Update Asset Support operation, but was removed to handle the updates.

In the `validate()` function (`source/go/lib/assettype/info.go`) include the assetTypeID already registered error but include the network and token type in the check.

# **Acceptance Criteria**

* While we are registering assets though xpress we are able to know if we have the same asset type id mismatch

nodes.description:
# Description

We made an unsuccessful attempt to enable asset type validation when adding a trusted destination. However, the validation was implemented in the wrong location, which shares the same code execution flow as `signed_organization_parse`. This causes conflicts, leading to [this issue](https://www.notion.so/anchorage/ERC20-Xpress-Special-Org-1595b28f309180048e4df21b6a7b68cc#1595b28f309180b3ae55d6a51446810c).

Therefore, we need to add the validation to `trusted_destination_add_t::apply`. After applying this change, we should remove the redundant backend check that prevents adding a trusted destination to the "special org." We must then test to ensure the environment remains stable.

# **Acceptance Criteria**

* The asset type validation is added to the trusted destination add
* We deploy a local environment, disable the backend check, and verify that everything continues to function correctly after adding the trusted destination to the special org.

# **Dependencies**

HSM
nodes.title: [HSM] Ensure asset_type is validated when executing a Add Trusted Destination org change
